newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty stabilises, finds new range.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty stabilises, finds new range.

text.p: The Polish zloty stabilised around Monday's fixing levels at about 0.75 percent above the parity rate after gentle early swings, dealers said.

Dealers said the zloty was likely to hold between 0.5 and 1.0 percent from parity in the near-future, with light foreign withdrawal from Polish papers expected whenever the zloty firmed past resistance and capital inflows when it hit support.

"This is a good initial range for the week, but it seems that upward pressure on the zloty has been slightly weaker, meaning that resistance may be strong," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
At 0845 GMT the zloty the zloty was at 0.77/0.74 percent from the parity rate against an early quote at 1.04/0.73.
It was at 3.2880/90 to the dollar, against the opening's 3.2800/00 and at 1.8840/45 to the mark, against 1.8780/40.
Some said that the zloty rebounded from this morning's lows as banks' cut currency exposure ahead of U.S. market holidays on July 4 to take advantage of higher yielding zloty deposits.

Dealers said foreigners may refrain from larger purchases of Polish debt instruments until after parliamentary elections in late September, when the thorny issue of next year's budget deficit plan could fianally start to be resolved.

"Foreigners may wait until after the elections with buying Polish paper because many do not believe that politicians would make unpopular decisions on tightning the fiscal policy before the polls," said Maciej Kwiatkowski of Societe Generale.
The central bank and the IMF last week called on the government to eliminate the budget deficit quickly or risk propelling Poland into a Czech-style finanacial crisis.

The government responded by saying it would sufficiently curb next year's budget gap to cool rampant domestic demand, but that a balanced budget was impossible in 1998. The cabinet is due to discuss next year's budget outlines later on Tuesday.
On the money market one-day rates slipped from early highs as some free cash flowed out into the market from the morning clearing session, dealers said.
Earlier rates spiraled upward as banks sought cash to pay back lombard credit taken at the end of June's reserve.
At 0905 GMT overnight rates were at 22.50/23.50 percent, down from opening's at 23.7/24.2 percent and tomorrow/next were at 22.65/23.80 percent, flat from 23.1/23.8 at 0650 GMT.
